name: serde (serde_derive typed deserialization)
baseline: RapidJSON DOM parser and nlohmann/json (JSON libraries in the same suite; no Cereal or Boost.Serialization comparison found)
workload: Parse a generated JSON file of 524,288 objects (each with x, y, z doubles, a name string and a nested opts array; json/generate_json.rb) and average the coordinates (kostya/benchmarks 'Json' test: parsing and simple calculating of values from a big JSON file); the Serde Typed row is serde_json::from_str into a struct with #[derive(Deserialize)] (serde_derive code generation) and the Serde Custom row adds a hand-written Visitor through #[serde(deserialize_with)].
claimed_speedup: Serde Typed (derive) 0.110 s and Serde Custom (derive plus visitor) 0.103 s vs RapidJSON 0.154 s (g++) and 0.194 s (clang++), and vs nlohmann/json 1.266 s (g++) and 1.182 s (clang++): about 1.4x-1.9x faster than default RapidJSON and about 10.7x-11.5x faster than nlohmann/json (derived from page data). Not faster than the closest declarative type-mapped C++ comparator in the suite, DAW JSON Link (0.085 s clang++, 0.089 s g++), nor than simdjson On-Demand (0.060-0.062 s).
compiler_and_flags: Rust (Serde rows): rustc 1.97.1, cargo build --release with RUSTFLAGS='-C target-cpu=native -C llvm-args=--x86-branches-within-32B-boundaries' and profile.release lto=true, codegen-units=1, panic=abort, strip=true; Cargo version requirements serde_json 1.0.150 and serde 1.0.228 (derive) with no extra serde_json features (no float_roundtrip). C++ baselines: g++ 16.1.0 and clang++ 22.1.8 with -Wall -Wextra -pedantic -Wcast-align -O3 -march=native -flto=auto -Wa,-mbranches-within-32B-boundaries -std=c++23 (clang++ also -stdlib=libc++); RapidJSON, nlohmann/json and simdjson cloned from their GitHub master at build time (kostya/benchmarks json/Makefile and common/commands.mk).
hardware: Intel(R) Xeon(R) E-2324G, Docker image based on Debian GNU/Linux forky/sid (kostya/benchmarks README, Environment section; table updated 2026-07-19)
tradeoffs: Rust-only framework: derive macros generate the (de)serializers at compile time (no runtime reflection), so a C++ project can only use it across an FFI or a separate process. Typed deserialization uses far less memory than a DOM (111.75 MiB base + 11.12 MiB for Serde Typed vs 113.21 + 123.44 MiB for g++ RapidJSON on the same page). Derive-generated code adds compile time and binary size (not measured here).
caveats: The serde repository itself has no benchmark or performance numbers (its README only says 'efficiently'); the only numbers found are the kostya/benchmarks Serde rows, which exercise serde's derive path through serde_json on JSON text. No comparison against Cereal, Boost.Serialization or a C++ reflection-based binary serializer was found (web searches surfaced only C++-only suites such as cpp-serializers and Rust-only suites); the baselines beaten here (RapidJSON, nlohmann/json) are DOM-style JSON parsers outside the listed baselines, hence baseline_in_list false. Not like for like: the typed rows skip the name and opts fields while the C++ DOM rows build the whole document; the DOM-style serde_json::Value row (0.557 s) is slower than RapidJSON DOM (0.154-0.194 s). The kostya build does not enable serde_json's float_roundtrip, so floats are parsed best-effort, as in default RapidJSON; RapidJSON Precise rows are 0.212 s (g++) and 0.262 s (clang++). The closest declarative, type-mapped C++ comparator DAW JSON Link is faster (0.085-0.089 s) and simdjson On-Demand is about 1.8x faster (0.060 s g++), so serde does not beat the best C++ typed parsers on this workload. The same suite and rows back the serde_json record (https://github.com/serde-rs/json) from this pass, so this record may fold into that one. Single workload, one machine, table updated 2026-07-19.
found_via: seed-record pass: started from https://github.com/serde-rs/serde (README has no benchmarks), followed the serde_json README Performance section to https://github.com/serde-rs/json-benchmark and https://github.com/kostya/benchmarks (Json section, Serde Typed and Serde Custom rows; json.rs/src/json_struct.rs and json_pull.rs).

name: serde_json (typed, #[derive(Deserialize)])
baseline: RapidJSON (DOM parser) and nlohmann/json; simdjson is faster
workload: Parse a generated JSON file of 524,288 objects (each with x, y, z doubles, a name string and a nested opts array; json/generate_json.rb) and average the coordinates (kostya/benchmarks 'Json' test: parsing and simple calculating of values from a big JSON file); the Serde Typed row is serde_json::from_str into a #[derive(Deserialize)] struct.
claimed_speedup: Rust Serde Typed 0.110 s vs RapidJSON 0.154 s (g++) and 0.194 s (clang++) and RapidJSON Precise 0.212 s (g++) and 0.262 s (clang++), and vs nlohmann/json 1.266 s (g++) and 1.182 s (clang++): about 1.4x-1.8x faster than default RapidJSON and about 10.7x-11.5x faster than nlohmann/json (derived from page data). Rust Serde Custom (derive plus hand-written visitor) 0.103 s. Not faster than simdjson On-Demand 0.060 s (g++) / 0.062 s (clang++) or DAW JSON Link 0.085-0.089 s; about equal to simdjson DOM 0.103-0.107 s. Rust Serde Untyped (serde_json::Value DOM) 0.557 s is about 2.1x-2.3x faster than nlohmann/json but about 2.9x-3.6x slower than RapidJSON DOM (derived from page data).
compiler_and_flags: Rust (Serde rows): rustc 1.97.1, cargo build --release with RUSTFLAGS='-C target-cpu=native -C llvm-args=--x86-branches-within-32B-boundaries' and profile.release lto=true, codegen-units=1, panic=abort, strip=true; Cargo version requirements serde_json 1.0.150 and serde 1.0.228 (derive) with no extra serde_json features (no float_roundtrip). C++ baselines: g++ 16.1.0 and clang++ 22.1.8 with -Wall -Wextra -pedantic -Wcast-align -O3 -march=native -flto=auto -Wa,-mbranches-within-32B-boundaries -std=c++23 (clang++ also -stdlib=libc++); RapidJSON, nlohmann/json and simdjson cloned from their GitHub master at build time (kostya/benchmarks json/Makefile and common/commands.mk).
hardware: Intel(R) Xeon(R) E-2324G, Docker image based on Debian GNU/Linux forky/sid (kostya/benchmarks README, Environment section; table updated 2026-07-19)
tradeoffs: Rust crate; a C++ project must reach it through an FFI or a separate process. Typed deserialization needs the target types known at compile time (derive), ignores unknown fields by default and uses far less memory than a DOM (111.75 MiB base + 11.12 MiB for Serde Typed vs 113.21 + 123.44 MiB for g++ RapidJSON and 447.88 MiB increase for g++ nlohmann/json on the same page). The untyped serde_json::Value DOM is much slower (0.557 s) and uses 839.75 MiB extra. float_roundtrip (exact float round-tripping) is an opt-in feature that costs about 2x float-parse speed per the crate's Cargo.toml comment.
caveats: 1) Not like for like: the typed Rust row skips the name and opts fields, while the C++ DOM rows build the whole document; the like-for-like DOM row (Serde Untyped, 0.557 s) loses to RapidJSON (0.154-0.194 s). 2) Float handling: the kostya Cargo.toml enables no float_roundtrip, so serde_json parses floats best-effort like default RapidJSON; the README itself notes that default RapidJSON has number-parsing inaccuracies, and only the Precise rows (0.212/0.262 s) are exact, so the 1.9x-2.4x margin over Precise is not a same-accuracy comparison. 3) simdjson On-Demand (0.060 s g++, 0.062 s clang++) is about 1.8x faster than Serde Typed (derived from page data) and DAW JSON Link (0.085-0.089 s) about 1.2x-1.3x faster, so serde_json is not the fastest JSON option here. 4) Single workload (large pretty-printed file, three double fields averaged) from one multi-language suite that is maintained by a third party; error bars shown, one machine. 5) The crate README performance claim ('500 to 1000 megabytes per second deserialization and 600 to 900 megabytes per second serialization ... competitive with the fastest C and C++ JSON libraries or even 30% faster for many use cases') carries no table; its linked https://github.com/serde-rs/json-benchmark (archived by its owner 2024-05-20; serde_json 1.0.72, rustc 1.59.0-nightly 2021-12-07, Intel Core i7-6600U, C++ built with -std=c++1z -O3 under clang 11.0.0 and gcc 10.1.0) shows serde_json DOM parse of 320/420/300 MB/s (canada/citm_catalog/twitter) slower than RapidJSON's 380-390/680-890/320-440 MB/s on all three files, DOM stringify faster on canada (430 vs 200-250 MB/s) and twitter (910 vs 600-870 MB/s) but slower on citm_catalog (560 vs 1090-1650 MB/s), and struct parse 580/710/550 MB/s with no C++ struct column labelled in the README. In that repo the Rust harness links jemalloc while the C++ harness uses the default allocator, the README's RapidJSON table does not say which columns are DOM or struct, and the committed cpp/main.cc benchmarks only canada.json (citm_catalog and twitter are commented out), so those rows are not reproducible as committed.
found_via: seed-record pass: started from https://github.com/serde-rs/json README (Performance section), then https://github.com/serde-rs/json-benchmark, then https://github.com/kostya/benchmarks (Json section, Rust Serde rows) and its json/Makefile, common/commands.mk, json.rs/Cargo.toml and test_*.cpp sources; one WebSearch for serde_json vs RapidJSON comparisons found no other suite with all three.
